back: Comparing the results and ratios of one business with another, ideally in the same trade and period.

front: Factors that make two businesses' ratios differ
back: Type of business, size, location, financing, accounting policies, age of assets, strategy.
Different accounting policies, year ends, sizes, types of business, one year's data only, limited information, historic cost.
Low net book value lowers capital employed, so ROCE looks higher.
Change profit and asset values for identical trading, so the ratios are not comparable.
Inventory, cash and payables on the two dates may differ, distorting liquidity and efficiency ratios.
Compare similar businesses, use several years, check accounting policies and year ends.

front: Is a higher margin always better?
back: No: a high-volume, low-margin business may earn more profit and a higher return than a low-volume, high-margin one.
